providers.what: The service that supplies Hermes with its AI brain — the place where the actual language model lives and does the thinking.
providers.why: You pick a provider so Hermes can talk to a model that fits your needs, budget, or privacy rules.
steps: Open the providers section in settings.
Choose a provider you have access to.
Pick a model from its list and save.
providers.gotcha: Some providers need an account or payment method first — a blank reply usually means the key isn't linked yet.

apikeys.what: A secret password that lets Hermes prove it's allowed to use a paid AI service.
apikeys.why: Without a key, Hermes can't reach most providers, so it can't answer or do work.
steps: Get a key from your provider's website.
Paste it into the API key field.
Save and test with a simple question.
apikeys.gotcha: Never share your key in chat or screenshots — anyone who sees it can spend your money.

tools.what: Built-in abilities that let Hermes actually do things, like running code or searching the web.
tools.why: Tools turn Hermes from a chat box into something that can act on the real world.
steps: Browse the list of available tools.
Toggle on the ones you want enabled.
Try a task that uses one, like a web search.
tools.gotcha: Enabling too many tools at once can confuse Hermes about which to use — start small.

skills.what: Reusable recipes that teach Hermes how to handle a specific type of job well.
skills.why: Skills save you from repeating instructions every time you want the same result.
steps: Look through the skills library.
Enable or load one that fits your task.
Ask Hermes to do the job and it follows the recipe.
skills.gotcha: A skill only helps if its description matches your request — vague asks may skip it.

mcp.what: A bridge that connects Hermes to other apps and outside services through a standard plug-in.
mcp.why: MCP lets Hermes reach tools and data living in programs you already use.
steps: Find an MCP server for the service you want.
Add its connection details in settings.
Turn it on and test a command.
mcp.gotcha: If the server isn't running, Hermes can't see it — check the connection is live first.

bots.what: Little automated helpers that can run Hermes tasks for you without you typing each time.
bots.why: Bots handle routine jobs or reply in chats so you don't have to be present.
steps: Create a new bot and give it a name.
Connect it to a channel or schedule.
Tell it what task to run.
bots.gotcha: A bot will keep doing its job on its own — double-check its instructions before letting it run freely.

memory.what: Hermes's notebook that remembers useful facts about you and past conversations.
memory.why: Memory lets Hermes pick up where it left off instead of starting blank every time.
steps: Open the memory section.
Add a note about a preference or fact.
Ask a follow-up question to see it recalled.
memory.gotcha: Too much saved memory clutters replies — clear out old or wrong notes now and then.

cron.what: A timer that tells Hermes to do a task automatically at times you choose.
cron.why: Cron runs jobs for you on a schedule, like a daily report, while you sleep.
steps: Open the schedule or cron section.
Write a task and pick when it should run.
Save and confirm it fires once to test.
cron.gotcha: Times usually follow a specific timezone — a job may run hours off from what you expect.

gateway.what: A door that lets Hermes talk to you through apps like Telegram or other chat platforms.
gateway.why: A gateway means you can message Hermes from your phone instead of a terminal.
steps: Open the gateway settings.
Connect a chat app using its setup steps.
Send a test message from that app.
gateway.gotcha: Messages from the gateway may need you to start the chat first before Hermes can reply.

config.what: The master settings file where all of Hermes's preferences are stored as text.
config.why: Editing the config lets you change many settings at once and back them up easily.
steps: Find the config file in your settings or folder.
Read the existing options.
Change one value and save to see the effect.
config.gotcha: A single typo in the config can stop Hermes from starting — keep a backup copy.
